$comment: DRAFT recipe, kept at the repository root because Melty reads it from there when the mashup is published from a GitHub link. Written against the recipe fields described in the publish brief; it has NOT been through validate_recipe or one_click_check, because melty.gg is not reachable from the build machine (see ra2-terror-strike/README.md, 'Still missing before this can be published'), so the schema could not be confirmed. Every value comes from a real file in this project: the component name is what tools/package.mjs produces, and the launch arguments are what dist/TerrorStrike.exe --help accepts.

components.description: The converter and launcher. Reads both games on the player's PC, writes generated files into the Red Alert 2 / Yuri's Revenge folder, then starts the game. Contains no game content.

checks.expects: exit code 0 and the line 'test build finished: clean' in the log
the log lists one 'companion: scripts/weapon_*.txt' line per weapon and one 'cameo *.shp' line per icon
rulesmd.ini, artmd.ini and five *.shp files exist in the host folder and are listed in terrorstrike-manifest.json

credits.what: Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2 and Yuri's Revenge, the host game
Counter-Strike: Source, the companion game whose weapon scripts and textures are converted

says: Four Counter-Strike operators join Red Alert 2 / Yuri's Revenge skirmish
Their weapons use the damage, clip, cycle time and range read from the player's own Counter-Strike: Source weapon scripts
Their sidebar icons are rendered from the player's own Counter-Strike: Source weapon textures
A T Bomber carries a C4 charge that detonates for 1200 damage across four cells
Combat pays: crates respawn in two minutes, money crates are worth 3000, free-unit crates hand out operators, ore no longer grows
Single player skirmish against the AI
Everything is generated on the player's PC from their own copies; nothing from either game is redistributed
